findings.title: Archived customers are offered in both sell-order customer pickers, and the new-draft modal preselects the alphabetically first customer, archived or not
findings.evidence: DesktopSellOrderDraft.tsx:106-115 fetches GET /api/customers with no status param and does setCustomerId(r.items[0].id). DesktopSellOrders.tsx:1184 fetches the same list for the editor. CustomerPicker (DesktopSellOrderDraft.tsx:505-511) filters only by the search text, never by `active`. The backend defaults status to 'all' and orders by name (apps/backend/src/routes/customers.ts:42,69), so archived rows come back. But the Customers panel promises the opposite on archive: i18n custArchiveBody = 'They will be hidden from new sell-order pickers but their history is preserved.' Because of the preselect, the sodBlockedNoCustomer blocker (line 164) can never fire while any customer exists.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager archives a defunct customer 'Acme Ltd'. Later another manager opens Inventory > New sell order. The picker already shows 'Acme Ltd' (first alphabetically). The manager fills prices and clicks Save draft without touching the customer, and the order is filed under the archived customer. Archived customers also stay pickable in the edit page's picker.
findings.proposed_fix: Request /api/customers?status=active (or filter c.active) for the pickers, keeping the order's current customer as a one-off option in the editor. Drop the r.items[0] preselect so the existing sodBlockedNoCustomer blocker asks for a choice.
findings.regression_test: A vitest/RTL test of DesktopSellOrderDraft with a mocked /api/customers returning [archived 'Acme', active 'Beta']: the picker lists only Beta, nothing is preselected, and clicking Save shows the no-customer blocker.

findings.title: Warehouse 'Active' toggle archives the warehouse on one click, with no confirmation and no in-app undo
findings.evidence: Toggle onChange={(v) => setActive(w.id, v)} at line 154 calls PATCH /api/warehouses/:id {active:false} right away (lines 56-66). The code's own comment says archiving removes the warehouse from every UI surface ('GET /api/warehouses no longer returns it'), and 'There is no in-app un-archive by design; reactivation is a direct DB edit.' The Delete path next to it has a two-step confirm (lines 422-484); archive has none. The toggle sits in each card's footer beside a disabled look-alike toggle.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager means to look at the disabled 'Accepting receipts' toggle and clicks 'Active' on the Denver card instead. The warehouse vanishes from the panel and from every warehouse picker (PO submit, transfers, pack lists). Getting it back takes a database edit.
findings.proposed_fix: Route active=false through a ConfirmDialog (the panel already imports the pattern from ./dialogs) that names the warehouse and says it can only be restored in the DB, or move archive into the edit modal's danger zone next to Delete.
findings.regression_test: An RTL test: clicking the Active toggle opens a confirm dialog and sends no PATCH until it is confirmed. Cancel leaves the card listed.

findings.title: After-sales case: changing status or adding a note silently discards unsaved Resolution-card edits
findings.evidence: move() (L283-297) and addNote() (L299-313) both finish with `await load()`. load() (L234-248) unconditionally calls setDraft({issue, resolution, amount, currency, assigneeId}) from the server copy. The Resolution card (L391-435) keeps its own draft with a separate 'Save details' button, and the page registers no useUnsavedGuard, so nothing warns that the draft is about to be replaced.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager types a refund amount of 120 and switches the currency to RMB, then clicks 'Resolve' in the header before 'Save details'. The status move succeeds, load() writes the server values back into the draft, the amount is gone, and the case is now Resolved and read-only (closed disables every field), so the amount can't be entered any more. Adding a timeline note after editing the issue text loses the edit the same way.
findings.proposed_fix: In load(), only reseed the draft when it is clean, for example by passing a flag from move/addNote and keeping the draft when `dirty`. Or block the status buttons while `dirty` ('save details first'), as DesktopEditOrder does for its Box check. Also call useUnsavedGuard(dirty) so Back and sidebar links ask first.
findings.regression_test: RTL: render CaseDetail with a mocked getAfterSalesCase, change the amount input, click a status action and confirm the modal (setAfterSalesStatus resolves). Assert that the amount input still shows the typed value, or that the move was blocked with a 'save first' message.

findings.title: Payments shows a CNY sell order's total with a $ sign, in the linked-row cell and in the Link picker
findings.evidence: Linked row renders fmtUSD(row.sellOrderTotal) (935-938) and the picker's SO tab renders fmtUSD(s.total) (1679). Sell orders can be CNY (migration 0065: currency_code IN ('USD','CNY')). bankTx.ts returns sellOrderCurrency (line 314) and SoSuggestion.currency (1241), but the page never reads either: PaymentRow has no sellOrderCurrency field, and its comment (186-189) calls the figure a 'USD total'. POST /link does not refuse a CNY sell order (bankTx.ts 523-531). The picker's 'exact' badge comes from comparing the CNY total with the USD bank amount (bankTx.ts 1227).
findings.failure_scenario: A manager links a $1,400 incoming PayPal payment to a ¥10,000 sell order. The row reads 'SO-123 $10,000.00 Payment', so the payment looks $8,600 short of a $10,000 order. In the picker a ¥1,400 order whose figure happens to equal the USD amount is badged 'Exact amount' and listed first.
findings.proposed_fix: Add sellOrderCurrency to PaymentRow and render fmtMoney(row.sellOrderTotal, row.sellOrderCurrency ?? 'USD', locale). In the picker use fmtMoney(s.total, s.currency, locale). [cross-lane, backend] Compute 'exact' only when so.currency_code = 'USD'.
findings.regression_test: Render PaymentTr with sellOrderTotal 10000 and sellOrderCurrency 'CNY' (renderToString) and expect '¥10,000.00', not '$'. Add a backend test that a CNY sell order never comes back with reason 'exact'.

findings.title: Host 'Authoritative' switch and capacity '+' start worker containers (Facebook logins) on a single click with no confirm
findings.evidence: authoritative(h) calls fleetApi.updateHost(h.host_id,{authoritative:!h.authoritative}) directly from the role=switch onClick (line 105-106); capacity(h,+1) (line 75-82, button at 113) saves immediately and only lowering past a running worker gets LowerCapacityDialog. Backend apps/backend/src/fleet/hosts.ts:240 workerCount returns 0 for a non-authoritative host and up to capacity once authoritative; its own comment says 'Every worker start is a Facebook login'. The file's header says observe-only exists 'so a freshly registered agent starts nothing by accident'.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager misclicks the switch on an observe-only host with capacity 8: on the agent's next poll the ERP answers count=min(8, free slots) and up to 8 containers boot, each restoring a session (a login in the vault ledger) - exactly what AGENTS.md's first rule forbids doing without reason. Each '+' click likewise boots one more worker.
findings.proposed_fix: Route turning authoritative ON (and raising capacity when it would raise the desired count) through a ConfirmDialogBody like LowerCapacityDialog, stating how many workers will start (desired count delta) and that each is a Facebook login. Turning it OFF can stay one click.
findings.regression_test: Render HostStrip with an observe-only host, click the switch, assert fleetApi.updateHost is not called until the confirm button in the dialog is pressed; same for the capacity '+' button.

findings.title: Account pool 'Resend login' queues a Facebook Re-login with one click, no confirm
findings.evidence: onSendLogin -> sendLogin(editor.no, workerId) -> poolApi.assign(...) (line 164-170), which per FleetAccounts.tsx:178-182 and the hint fpSendLoginHint ('writes the login into the worker vault and queues re-login') queues Re-login. The button that fires it (accountPool/AccountEditor.tsx:222-232) has only a title tooltip. Elsewhere the same action is guarded: ReloginButton (FleetAccounts.tsx:144-171) opens a confirm modal explaining the login.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager opening an account in the editor clicks 'Resend login to homelab-3' to see what it does; the worker immediately re-enters the password/2FA, risking a checkpoint on an account that was healthy - a login AGENTS.md says must never happen without a reason.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate onSendLogin behind the same confirm used by ReloginButton (or reuse ReloginButton's modal body): name the worker, say it is a Facebook login, and only then call sendLogin. Note: the button markup lives in accountPool/AccountEditor.tsx (possibly another lane); the wiring is here.
findings.regression_test: Render FacebookAccountPool as manager with a fleet account, open the editor, click 'fpSendLogin' and assert poolApi.assign is not called before a confirm.

findings.title: Submit form drops queued line photos and buffered evidence files on navigation/reload without a prompt
findings.evidence: useUnsavedGuard(lines.some(l => !l._confirmed && (!!l.brand || !!l.description))) is the only guard. It ignores photos.queuedFor(cid) (failed or not-yet-flushed line photos), evidenceFiles (line 206, buffered locally and uploaded only on submit) and the `unfinished` state. doSubmit (lines 719-727) explicitly keeps the user on the page because 'Those Files are the only copy of those pictures', but after a submit every line is _confirmed, so the guard is false exactly in that state.
findings.failure_scenario: Purchaser submits a PO; the line photo upload fails, the page shows 'Retry N photos' and stays. They click a sidebar link (or reload/close the tab): no unsaved prompt fires, the File objects are gone and the photos are lost for good. Same for evidence files dropped onto a PO whose lines were all confirmed one by one: a reload before Submit loses them silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the dirty flag: dirty = unconfirmed filled line || evidenceFiles.length > 0 || unfinished !== null || lines.some(l => photos.queuedFor(l._cid).length > 0).
findings.regression_test: Component test: render OrderForm, mock persistLines success and uploadLinePhoto failure, submit, then assert hasUnsavedChanges('/purchase-orders') is true; likewise after adding an evidence file with all lines confirmed.

findings.title: [cross-lane] List memory (usePersisted) survives logout, so the next user inherits the previous user's inventory selection, filters and search
findings.evidence: DesktopInventory keeps filter/search/warehouse/attrs/sort and the selection (Set of lot ids + Map of full InventoryRow incl. unit_cost) in usePersisted, backed by the module-level `mem` Map in lib/listMemory.ts:13. App.tsx remounts the shell on user change (key=user.id) precisely to drop the previous user's state, but `mem` is module scope and clearLocalAuthState (lib/auth.tsx:12) never clears it. Same for DesktopShipping scope/status/carrier/search (DesktopShipping.tsx:63-66) and the fleet sort.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager A selects 30 lots and searches 'DDR5' on Inventory, logs out; manager B logs in on the same tab. Inventory opens with A's search term, filters and the floating bar 'N lines / $X est. revenue'; B can press Create sell order and draft a sell order out of A's picks without having chosen them. A purchaser logging in after a manager sees the manager's search/filters applied to their own list.
findings.proposed_fix: Export a clearPersisted() from lib/listMemory.ts that empties `mem` and call it from clearLocalAuthState (and on login when the user id changes).
findings.regression_test: Unit test: usePersisted('k', x) set to y, call logout path (clearLocalAuthState), remount -> value is initial x.

findings.title: Manual market price dialog saves $0 from an empty field, and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits again while a save is in flight
findings.evidence: save() runs `const n = Number(price); if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 0) return;`. Number('') is 0, so a blank field passes, and so does the Save button's disabled check (line 771). The dialog opens blank for any row with lastPrice null (line 702). The overlay's onKeyDown at line 728 calls save() on Cmd/Ctrl+Enter without checking `saving`. The backend accepts 0 (apps/backend/src/routes/market.ts:454-456) and records it as the last sell price and a recentPrices point.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager opens Update price on a never-sold part and presses Save, or clears the field to retype and hits Cmd+Enter. A $0 'last sell' is recorded, the row's sparkline and staleness reset, and the Max-buy basis can drop to 0. Pressing Cmd+Enter twice quickly posts two manual-price datapoints.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a blank or whitespace field as invalid (price.trim() === '' fails the check), require n > 0 unless zero is truly wanted, and guard the key handler with `if (saving) return`.
findings.regression_test: An RTL test: open the dialog on a row with lastPrice null. Save is disabled and Cmd+Enter posts nothing. With a valid price, two quick Cmd+Enter presses produce exactly one POST.

findings.title: Expanded market row draws an SVG full of NaN and '$Infinity' tick labels when the item has fewer than 2 recent prices
findings.evidence: DetailExpand always renders <DualLineChart sell={sellHistory} cost={[]} /> (line 574). DualLineChart has no length guard, unlike Sparkline (line 21). With sell=[], max=Math.max()=-Infinity and min=Infinity*0.85, so the ticks read '$-Infinity'/'$NaN'/'$Infinity' and every path coordinate is NaN. With one price, x(i) divides by (sell.length - 1) = 0, so it is NaN as well. Brand-new or manually added rows have an empty recentPrices.
findings.failure_scenario: Clicking a newly tracked item opens a detail card whose chart axis reads '$Infinity / $NaN / $-Infinity' with broken paths, and React logs NaN-attribute warnings.
findings.proposed_fix: When sell.length < 2, render the 'no price history' empty state instead of the chart (the same guard Sparkline uses).
findings.regression_test: A renderToString of DetailExpand with recentPrices [] and with [one point]: the output contains no 'NaN' or 'Infinity'.

findings.title: Market infinite scroll retries a failed page in a tight loop for as long as the sentinel stays visible
findings.evidence: loadMore depends on [loadingMore, ...]. A failure runs handleFetchError, and then finally setLoadingMore(false) gives loadMore a new identity. useSentinel (lib/useSentinel.ts:16-26) re-creates the IntersectionObserver on every onHit identity change, and a sentinel already in view fires immediately, so loadMore runs again. Nothing backs off. The error dialog queue dedupes the message, but every attempt makes a network request and a reportClientError call.
findings.failure_scenario: With the backend returning 500 for offset=100 (or the network down), scrolling to the bottom of the Market list sends request after request, each failure posting a client-error report, until the user scrolls away or leaves the page.
findings.proposed_fix: Remember a failed offset (an error state) and stop arming the sentinel until the user clicks a 'Retry' row, or the query changes.
findings.regression_test: Mock api.get to reject for offset>0 and an IntersectionObserver that reports intersecting: after one failure, no second request goes out without user action.

findings.title: New-sell-order draft modal has no unsaved guard: Escape, a backdrop click, X or Cancel throws away the typed prices, and X/Cancel stay live during save
findings.evidence: The Modal's onClose (line 207) closes on Escape and on a backdrop click (components/Modal.tsx:35,59-61), guarded only by `saving`. The header X (line 226) and footer Cancel (line 436) call onClose directly, even while saving. The component never calls useUnsavedGuard, although per-line prices, qty, currency, receiver and notes are all edited here. The sell-order edit page does guard (DesktopSellOrders.tsx:1316). The pool AccountEditor (accountPool/AccountEditor.tsx:108-110) has the same gap for typed passwords, TOTP keys and cookies.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager prices 30 lines in the draft and presses Escape to dismiss the customer search. If the picker isn't open, Escape closes the whole modal and every price is lost. Clicking X mid-save closes the modal while the POST still lands, so a draft gets created that the user believes was cancelled.
findings.proposed_fix: Track dirty (lines/prices/notes/currency changed from their initial state), call useUnsavedGuard(dirty), route every close through confirmDiscard(), and disable X/Cancel while saving.
findings.regression_test: An RTL test: edit a unit price, press Escape, and the discard confirm appears with the modal still mounted. While saving, X is disabled.

findings.title: Internal-transaction record deletes on a single click, with no confirmation
findings.evidence: The 'Delete' button (line 358) calls destroy() at once, which sends DELETE /api/internal-transactions/:id. The backend removes the record and releases every member through ON DELETE SET NULL (apps/backend/src/routes/internalTx.ts:314-321). The title, note and grouping are gone, and nothing restores them. It sits right next to 'Add transaction' and does not check the unsaved guard either.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager reaching for 'Add transaction' clicks 'Delete' next to it, and a documented Mercury-to-PayPal transfer group and its explanatory note are destroyed.
findings.proposed_fix: Ask through ConfirmDialog (as PaymentIgnoreRules does for its rules) and disable the button while the request is pending.
findings.regression_test: An RTL test: clicking Delete shows a confirm, and no DELETE goes out until it is confirmed.

findings.title: Facebook Account pool tab stays on a skeleton for good after the snapshot fetch fails
findings.evidence: wantPool = poolOpen && !pool, and the effect runs poolApi.snapshot().then(setPool).catch(handleFetchError). After a failure, pool stays null, wantPool stays true and the dependency never changes, so nothing retries. Lines 125-128 then render <FormSkeleton/> forever. This is the purchasers' only view on this page.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient 502 on /api/facebook-pool/snapshot shows one error dialog, and then the pool area shows loading bars indefinitely. A purchaser has to reload the whole app to take an account.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep an error state and render an inline failure with a Retry button (or bump a retry key), instead of the skeleton.
findings.regression_test: Mock poolApi.snapshot to reject once: the tab shows a retry affordance, not FormSkeleton, and Retry loads the pool.

findings.title: Customer list is capped at 200 by name: the pickers and the Customers panel totals silently drop everyone after it
findings.evidence: GET /api/customers clamps the limit to 200 by default (apps/backend/src/routes/customers.ts:45) with ORDER BY c.name LIMIT and no cursor. The callers never pass limit or page: CustomersPanel.tsx:38 (its totals at lines 72-78 and the 'active of total' header sum the returned array), DesktopSellOrderDraft.tsx:107 and DesktopSellOrders.tsx:1184 (the pickers). Today this is latent unless the table holds more than 200 rows.
findings.failure_scenario: Once there are 201 or more customers, 'Zeta Corp' can't be found in either sell-order picker (and an order already filed under it shows the placeholder in the editor's picker). The Customers panel undercounts the totals, Lifetime and Outstanding with no hint of truncation.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the panel ask for the server's maximum and show a 'showing N of M' note, or add keyset paging / server-side search for the pickers, and compute the panel's sums server-side.
findings.regression_test: Backend test plus a UI test: with 201 seeded customers, a picker search for the 201st name finds it, and the panel total reads 201.

findings.title: Switching a sell order's currency keeps the typed numbers, so USD prices are reinterpreted as CNY with no conversion or warning
findings.evidence: CurrencyPicker onChange={cur => setDraft({ ...draft, currency: cur })} leaves every line's unitPrice (native) as it was, and save() resends the lines unchanged (lines 1429-1442). The backend takes the new numbers as native prices in the new currency (apps/backend/src/routes/sellOrders.ts:762-771). The new-draft modal does the same (DesktopSellOrderDraft.tsx:254, with prices pre-seeded from the USD sellPrice at line 97). Its 'adjusted' list-price hint is shown only for USD (line 303), so nothing flags it. The backend comment says this is intended ('new native prices must come with it'); the risk is that the UI never points it out.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager flips an order from USD to CNY expecting the system to convert, and saves. A $1,000 line becomes ¥1,000 (about $140). The order total drops sevenfold, and the only cue is the small USD-equivalent line.
findings.proposed_fix: On a currency change, either convert the draft prices at the loaded FX rate, or show a blocking notice ('prices are now in CNY — re-enter them') and highlight unchanged prices until they are edited.
findings.regression_test: An RTL test: on a USD order, switching to CNY either rescales unitPrice by fx.oneUsdInQuote or shows the re-enter notice before Save is allowed.

findings.title: Expanded internal-transaction record beyond the first 200 rows loses its unsaved title/note when a member is added or removed
findings.evidence: addMember/removeMember call onChanged = reload(). reload's first page does setFeed({rows: items}) and replaces the whole list with page 1 (limit 200) before later pages append. A record open on page 2 or later drops out of feed.rows, its RecordTr/RecordDetailPanel unmounts, and when its page lands again the panel remounts from the server. The keepDraft fix (FE-16) covers only records that stay mounted.
findings.failure_scenario: With 200+ records, a manager opens an older record, types a note, then attaches its second leg. The panel flickers away and comes back with the saved note, and the typed text is gone without the discard prompt (the guard unregisters on unmount).
findings.proposed_fix: Make member changes refetch only that record and patch its row in place, instead of a full keyset reload. Or keep the old rows until the reload's pages have replaced them.
findings.regression_test: Mock 250 records, open #230, type a note, add a member: the textarea still holds the typed note.

findings.title: Watch page keeps the previous pool account's secrets, and their revealed state, after the worker's account changes
findings.evidence: The effect keyed on accountNo (L48-55) starts poolApi.snapshot() without first resetting `pool` to {kind:'loading'}, so until the snapshot lands the panel still renders the old account's login, password, 2FA code and Type buttons. WatchAccountPanel (watchAccount.tsx:60) has no key and holds `revealed` in state. A password revealed for account A therefore shows in clear for account B, and toggleReveal's audit('revealed') (watchAccount.tsx:111) never fires for B.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager watches a parked worker and reveals its password. The 30 s poll (or the 3 s poll during a re-login) returns the worker on a different pool account. For the length of the snapshot fetch, Type/Copy send account A's password or 2FA code into a browser now signing in as B. After that, B's password shows unmasked with no 'revealed' row in the pool ledger.
findings.proposed_fix: In the effect, setPool({kind:'loading'}) before fetching. Pass key={accountNo ?? 'none'} to WatchAccountPanel (or reset `revealed` when the account's `no` changes) so a reveal never carries across accounts.
findings.regression_test: RTL: render WatchAccountPanel with pool ok/account no=1, click Show password, then rerender with account no=2. Assert the password is masked again, and that poolApi.event is called when it is revealed for no=2.

findings.title: Tracker analytics: a slow response for the old window can overwrite the new one, and one failed background refresh blanks the card
findings.evidence: load() = `trackerApi.analytics(win).then(setData).catch(() => setData('unavailable'))` has no liveness or generation guard, and the effect cleanup (L43-46) only clears the timer and listener. The 60 s refresh and the visibilitychange refresh use the same catch, so a single transient error replaces good data with 'unavailable' and the MissedCard disappears (L74).
findings.failure_scenario: The user clicks 30d while the 7d request is still in flight. If 30d answers first and 7d second, the 30d tab stays selected while the KPIs, chart and tables show 7d numbers. Separately, a single 502 from the tracker proxy during the periodic refresh wipes the whole analytics section until the next successful poll.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a `let live = true` captured per effect run (or compare the response's `window` with the current `win`) before calling setData. On a refresh failure, keep the existing data and only set 'unavailable' when nothing has loaded yet.
findings.regression_test: Vitest + RTL with fake timers: mock analytics('7d') to resolve after analytics('30d'), click 30d, flush both, and assert the rendered window label or KPI comes from the 30d payload. Then make a refresh reject and assert the previous KPIs stay rendered.

findings.title: Inventory editor: the floating save bar's Save stays enabled on an archived line
findings.evidence: The header Save is `disabled={!dirty || saving || archived}` (L351), but the save-bar Save is only `disabled={saving}` (L451). No input is disabled when archived, so the draft can become dirty and the save bar appears.
findings.failure_scenario: On an Archived line (its PO is archived), the user edits the sell price. The header Save is greyed out, but the bottom bar's Save is live. Clicking it sends a PATCH that the backend refuses, and the user gets an error dialog instead of the archived banner's explanation.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the save-bar button the same `disabled={saving || archived}` (or hide the save bar when archived), and ideally disable the inputs when archived.
findings.regression_test: RTL: mock GET /api/inventory/:id with status 'Archived', change the sell price, and assert both Save buttons are disabled.

findings.title: PO editor: Archive and Unarchive leave the page and drop unsaved edits without the discard confirmation
findings.evidence: Unarchive (L1355-1364) and the archive modal's confirm (L2070-2083) call onSaved(), which navigate()s back to the list. navigate() counts as a self-navigation, so the leave guard doesn't ask, and neither handler checks `dirty`. The Box check button right next to them refuses with bcSaveFirst when dirty (L1338), and the In Transit handoff does the same (L1243).
findings.failure_scenario: A manager edits several unit costs and the fee on a PO, then archives it before saving. The archive succeeds, the page returns to the list, and the edits are silently lost even though useUnsavedGuard(dirty) is registered.
findings.proposed_fix: Before opening the archive modal or calling unarchive, check `dirty`: either show showErrorDialog(t('bcSaveFirst')), or await confirmDiscard() and stop if it resolves false.
findings.regression_test: RTL: render DesktopEditOrder with a canArchive order, edit the fee input, click Archive and confirm. Assert archiveOrder was not called (or that the discard dialog appeared first).

findings.title: Transfer modal: one fully committed lot blocks the whole batch, with no way to drop it
findings.evidence: qty defaults to movable(it) = qty - committedQty (L45-47), which is 0 for a fully committed lot. anyInvalidQty treats n < 1 as invalid for every line (L69-72), and the modal has no control to remove a line. DesktopInventory.buildTransferItems (DesktopInventory.tsx:562) includes every selected lot, whatever its committed_qty.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager selects 12 lots to move to another warehouse, and one is fully held by an open sell order. The modal shows '/0' for that lot, and Transfer only shows the 'qty out of range' dialog. The manager has to close the modal, find and deselect the lot, and start over. The hint doesn't say which lot is the problem.
findings.proposed_fix: Leave lots with movable === 0 out of the payload (show them greyed out as 'held by sell orders'), or add a per-line remove button. Only treat n < 1 as an error when movable > 0.
findings.regression_test: RTL: render with two items, one with qty 5 / committedQty 5. Pick a destination, click Transfer, and assert the POST went out with only the movable line.

findings.title: Buyer network tree shows a skeleton forever when the buyer fetch fails
findings.evidence: setTree(null) and then `leadsApi.buyer(current).then(r => ..., handleFetchError)`. The rejection path never sets an error state, and the render shows <ListSkeleton> whenever `!tree` (L69).
findings.failure_scenario: The tree request for a buyer fails (network drop, or a 5xx from the leads API). A toast flashes, but the tree card keeps its loading skeleton indefinitely, so it looks like it's still loading and the only way to retry is to click a different buyer.
findings.proposed_fix: Track a 'failed' state in the rejection handler and render an error line with a retry action instead of the skeleton.
findings.regression_test: RTL: mock leadsApi.buyer to reject and assert an error message replaces the skeleton.

findings.title: Clickable table rows with no keyboard path: PO line drawer and inventory product groups
findings.evidence: DesktopEditOrder opens a line's LineDrawer only through `<tr onClick={() => setActiveIdx(i)}>` (L1465-1475), with no tabIndex, role or key handler, and the row has no other control that opens the drawer. InventoryProductTable.tsx:190-193 does the same for expanding a product group: the chevron is a bare <Icon>, not a button, so the lots and their Quick view/Edit buttons can't be reached by keyboard.
findings.failure_scenario: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user can't open any PO line to edit qty, cost or serials, and can't expand a product group in the grouped inventory view to reach a lot's Edit action.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the item cell (or the chevron in InventoryProductTable) a <button> with aria-expanded, or give the row tabIndex=0, role='button' and an Enter/Space handler.
findings.regression_test: RTL: focus the row's button, press Enter, and assert the drawer opens or the group's lot table renders.

findings.title: A non-USD bank row's amount is formatted as dollars
findings.evidence: The amount cell is fmtSigned(row.amount, locale), which always prefixes '$' (format.ts:29-31). Legs (1133) and pair candidates (1848) do the same. The row carries currency (bankTx.ts 305), and the page knows it: it shows a 'payForeignChip' with that currency at 881-885.
findings.failure_scenario: A €250 PayPal receipt shows '+$250.00' next to an 'EUR' chip. Anyone scanning the amount column for money in reads it as dollars.
findings.proposed_fix: Use (n<0?'−':'+') + fmtMoney(Math.abs(n), row.currency ?? 'USD', locale) for the row and its legs.
findings.regression_test: Render a row with currency 'EUR' and assert the amount cell contains no '$'.

findings.title: Every Payments action reloads only the first page, so rows loaded by scrolling vanish and the open row collapses
findings.evidence: afterMutation (464) calls reload(), and reload fetches /api/bank-transactions with no cursor and replaces the feed with setFeed(r) (423-424). The page size is 50 (bankTx.ts 136: clampLimit(...,50,200)). Pages appended by loadMore are dropped, and the expanded row (openId) unmounts if it lived past row 50.
findings.failure_scenario: On the All tab a manager scrolls to row 120, expands it, assigns an owner or saves a note. The list collapses back to 50 rows, the expanded row with its half-typed note draft is gone, and the scroll position jumps. The note editor seeds its draft from the row, so any unsaved text is lost.
findings.proposed_fix: After a mutation, refetch the same depth: walk cursors until the loaded row count is covered, or pass limit=min(200, rows.length). Alternatively, patch the acted row in place and refresh only the stats.
findings.regression_test: Component test with a mocked api: load 2 pages, call act() on a row from page 2, and assert the feed still holds more than 50 rows and openId is unchanged.

findings.title: Payments tiles can show a stale direction's counts: refreshStats has no request guard
findings.evidence: refreshStats is api.get(stats?direction=…).then(setStats) with no reqId or alive check, unlike reload (422-424), which drops superseded responses. The comment at 412-415 promises that the tile and the rows can never disagree.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager flips the direction select Out → All → Out quickly, or clicks the Refunds tile and then another tile. If the earlier stats response lands last, the Unlinked tile shows the other direction's count and amount over a list that disagrees.
findings.proposed_fix: Mirror reload: const id = ++statsReq.current; then setStats only if id === statsReq.current.
findings.regression_test: Mock two stats requests that resolve out of order and assert the later request's numbers are the ones rendered.

findings.title: Link picker spins 'Loading…' forever when its suggestions request fails
findings.evidence: The effect calls setRows(null) and then api.get(...).then(setRows).catch(handleFetchError). On failure rows stays null, which renders t('payMoreLoading') (1659-1660). RecordPicker (1717-1720) has the same pattern. MatchList (1456) and PairPicker (1813) both setRows([]) on error.
findings.failure_scenario: A 500 or timeout on /suggestions while switching to the Commission tab leaves the popover reading 'Loading…' indefinitely after an error toast. The manager cannot tell it apart from a slow request.
findings.proposed_fix: In the catch, when id === reqId.current, setRows([]) and set an error flag, as MatchList does.
findings.regression_test: Mock api.get to reject and assert the picker leaves the loading state.

findings.title: Clients page reports a failed load as an empty book and invites adding a client
findings.evidence: reload() catches with handleFetchError but still runs .finally(() => setLoaded(true)) (67-68). data stays null, so counts.total is 0, and the card renders EmptyState with total=0, i.e. 'cliEmptyNoneTitle' plus an Add client button (198-202, 309-316).
findings.failure_scenario: A transient /api/suppliers failure (or a 500 on one of the 500-row pages loadBook walks) shows a purchaser 'No clients yet', with a primary button to add one. They re-create a supplier who already exists. The header also reads '0 clients'.
findings.proposed_fix: Track an error state: on failure render a retry card instead of EmptyState, and keep the skeleton while data is null.
findings.regression_test: Mock api.get to reject and assert the 'cliEmptyNoneTitle' copy is absent and a retry is offered.

findings.title: Client drawer stays on 'Loading…' forever when the client can't be read, e.g. from a deep link
findings.evidence: load() is api.get(`/api/suppliers/${id}`).then(setC).catch(handleFetchError). While c is null the modal renders only t('loadingApp') (35-41). Since FE-12, /clients/:id opens this drawer straight from a pasted URL.
findings.failure_scenario: A purchaser opens a client link a colleague pasted for a client outside their scope, or one that was deleted. The request 403s or 404s, a toast flashes, and the drawer sits on 'Loading…' with no message.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep an error state. On 404/403 close the drawer (navigate('/clients')) or show 'not found' inside it.
findings.regression_test: Mount ClientDrawer with api.get rejecting with ApiError 404 and assert the loading text is replaced.

findings.title: Transfers shows 'no transfers' while it loads, and the previous filter's list after a failed load
findings.evidence: orders starts as [] and there is no loading flag, so the first render, and every load that fails, renders t('transfersEmpty') (171-172). On a filter change, the old filter's orders stay on screen until the new walk's first page lands (108). If that load fails (110), only a toast shows and the old list stays under the new filter's highlighted button.
findings.failure_scenario: A warehouse user switches Pending → Received on a slow link and briefly sees the pending orders, Confirm buttons included, under 'Received'. If the request fails, that stays. On first open they see 'No transfers' before the real list arrives.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a loaded/error state. Clear orders, or show a skeleton, when the filter changes, and render the empty text only after a successful load.
findings.regression_test: Mock a slow then failing load and assert neither the empty copy nor the previous filter's rows render as data.

findings.title: Seen-alerts card blanks to 'unavailable' on any single failed 60-second refresh
findings.evidence: load() is trackerApi.seen().then(setData).catch(() => setData('unavailable')), and it reruns every 60 s and on visibility change (26-35). useFleetPoll (fleet/shared.tsx:105) keeps the last good answer on a failed re-read; this card throws it away.
findings.failure_scenario: One proxy hiccup to the Reddit tracker replaces a populated read-receipts table with 'trkSeenUnavailable' until the next minute's poll.
findings.proposed_fix: On error, keep prev unless prev is null: setData(p => (p && p !== 'unavailable' ? p : 'unavailable')).
findings.regression_test: Resolve once, then reject on the refresh, and assert the people table is still rendered.

findings.title: General settings starts on invented values; a toggle flipped before or without the load overwrites the stored AI-review object
findings.evidence: State starts on hardcoded placeholders: domain 'recycleservers.io', timezone LA, aiReview = AI_REVIEW_DEFAULT with enabled:false and model:null (90-99). These stay forever if GET /api/workspace fails, since the catch only toasts (121). updAi sends the whole object built from current state: persist({ po_ai_review: { ...data.aiReview, ...patch } }) (146-150). Text fields persist on every blur (175, 179).
findings.failure_scenario: A manager opens Settings while /api/workspace is slow or failing and toggles 'Web lookup'. The PATCH writes { enabled:false, model:null, maxCostPerPoUsd:0.5, webLookup }, which turns off a PO AI review that was enabled and erases the custom model. Blurring the Workspace name field also saves the placeholder name.
findings.proposed_fix: Hold data as null until the GET lands (render a skeleton), and disable the controls on load failure. Send only the changed AI-review key, or merge on the server.
findings.regression_test: Mock GET to reject, toggle webLookup, and assert no PATCH is sent, or that it carries only webLookup.

findings.title: Edit cities: pressing Enter in the 'add your own city' boxes submits the whole form instead of adding the city
findings.evidence: The slug, name and radius inputs (198-206) sit inside <form onSubmit={submit}> (150), and the Add button is type='button' with onClick={addOwn} (207). Enter in a text input therefore fires submit, which saves the current list (133) and closes the modal through onSaved, discarding the typed slug and name.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager who already removed one city types a new slug and name and presses Enter. The worker's config is saved without the new city, the modal closes, and the typed city is lost. They have to reopen the modal, and every save rewrites that worker's config.
findings.proposed_fix: Handle onKeyDown Enter on those three inputs: preventDefault, then addOwn(). Or move the add row out of the form.
findings.regression_test: Render EditCitiesModal, type into the slug input, press Enter, and assert saveCities was not called and the chip was added.

findings.title: Line drawer: closing during an in-flight Confirm lets the late onClose close the next line's drawer
findings.evidence: confirmLine awaits onConfirmLine() and then calls onClose() (254-257). Cancel (762), the X (356) and the backdrop (277) stay enabled while confirming. The parent's onClose is setActiveIdx(null) (DesktopSubmit.tsx:1262) and Escape closes too (DesktopSubmit.tsx:677).
findings.failure_scenario: On the edit page a purchaser clicks Confirm on line 3, which saves slowly, then presses Escape and opens line 4 to keep going. When line 3's save resolves, its stale onClose sets activeIdx to null and line 4's drawer slams shut mid-entry. Remove product is also enabled mid-save.
findings.proposed_fix: Track mounted/close intent: skip onClose if the drawer already closed. Or disable Cancel/X/backdrop/Remove while confirming.
findings.regression_test: Make onConfirmLine a deferred promise, close the drawer, open another, resolve, and assert the second stays open.

findings.title: Line drawer keeps showing the typed Total cost while the line is saved at qty × the rounded unit cost
findings.evidence: Typing a total sets unitCost = +(total/qty).toFixed(2) and totalCost = the typed string (681-686). The field then displays line.totalCost (680). line.totalCost is display-only: nothing in DesktopSubmit or DesktopEditOrder sends it. Meanwhile the header shows fmtUSD(qty*cost) (351).
findings.failure_scenario: A purchaser buys 3 sticks for $100 and types 100 in Total. The field keeps showing 100.00, but unit cost becomes 33.33 and the PO records $99.99. The drawer header in the same panel says $99.99, so the PO total is a cent off what was agreed.
findings.proposed_fix: After deriving the unit, show qty*unit (clear the override), or warn when total ≠ qty × unit. If exact lot totals matter, carry them through the lot-price path rather than a per-line display string.
findings.regression_test: Unit test: qty 3, type total 100, and assert the displayed total equals 3 × the unit, or that a mismatch warning shows.

findings.title: [cross-lane] Logout keeps page memory and the members cache, so the next user inherits them without a reload
findings.evidence: clearLocalAuthState resets lookups, workspace, warehouses and AI models, but not listMemory's module-level `mem` (listMemory.ts:13) or useManagers' `cache` (useManagers.ts:20, 60 s TTL). This lane's pages keep user-specific state there: DesktopPayments' search q and assignee (344-354), DesktopClients' filter (36). useMemberNames notes that includeInactive is 'a manager's read'.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager A filters Payments by search 'acme' and assignee B, logs out, and manager C logs in on the same tab: C lands on a filtered queue they didn't set. A purchaser who logs in within 60 s of a manager is served the cached includeInactive member list.
findings.proposed_fix: Call a reset for listMemory (mem.clear()) and forgetMembers() from clearLocalAuthState.
findings.regression_test: Set a persisted value and call logout(), then assert usePersisted returns its initial value.

findings.title: Analysis 'Alerts by city' alert rate is always blank: stale 1000-row guard, and a truncated read is summed as complete
findings.evidence: FleetAnalysisTab reads fleetApi.tasks({state:'done', since:14d}). A non-queue read is capped at HISTORY_LIMIT=5000 (apps/backend/src/fleet/tasks.ts:28,67) and the route signals truncation only via the X-Fleet-Truncated header (routes/fleet.ts:106), which lib/fleet.ts tasks() discards. alertsByCity (fleet/fleetBoard.ts:619) only computes rate when tasks.length < 1000, a leftover of the old LIST_LIMIT, and always shows the summed 'reviewed'.
findings.failure_scenario: With ~212 cities x 2 items searched daily, 14 days is several thousand done tasks: every 1000-4999-row read hides every rate ('-') even though the data is complete, and at >5000 rows the Reviewed column silently undercounts (older days cut) while Alerts covers all 14 days.
findings.proposed_fix: Have fleetApi.tasks surface the truncated header (or return {tasks,truncated}); in alertsByCity replace `tasks.length < 1000` with `!truncated`, and mark/blank Reviewed when truncated.
findings.regression_test: Unit test alertsByCity with 1500 complete done tasks -> rate non-null; with truncated=true -> rate null and reviewed flagged.

findings.title: Tasks tab 'Today (Eastern time)' range starts at UTC midnight
findings.evidence: sinceFor('today') returns new Date(now).toISOString().slice(0,10)+'T00:00:00.000Z' - UTC midnight - while the label fleetRange_today is '今天（美东时间）' / Today (Eastern) and the belt uses easternClock.
findings.failure_scenario: At 21:00 EDT (01:00 UTC next day) 'Today' shows only the last hour of tasks; at 10:00 EDT it includes 20:00-24:00 of yesterday. The table count and footer then misreport today's work.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute Eastern midnight (e.g. the same helper the belt/funnel use, America/New_York) and send that instant as `since`.

findings.title: Worker page 'Search a city now' dialog: disabled-city default leaves submit dead, and no items gives a false success
findings.evidence: SearchCityDialog passes initial = detail.cities[0]?.slug (cities the worker searched, latest first, possibly since disabled). SearchNowDialog (FleetTasksTab.tsx:506-509) uses it as the select value while options list only enabled cities, so city===null and the submit is disabled while the select visually shows the first enabled city. If no item is enabled, item='both', chosen=[] and submit runs Promise.allSettled([]) then shows fleetSearchNowDone; the Tasks tab disables its button for items.length===0 but the worker page (line 162) does not.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager opens Search now on a worker whose last city was disabled: the dialog shows 'Austin' selected but the button is greyed with no reason; with all items disabled a success toast says the city was queued when nothing was sent.
findings.proposed_fix: In SearchNowDialog fall back to enabled[0] when `initial` is not enabled; disable submit (and the worker-page button) when items is empty.
findings.regression_test: Render SearchNowDialog with initial set to a disabled slug -> submit enabled for enabled[0]; with items=[] -> submit disabled.

findings.title: Log contact schedules the next call one day off in the evening (local date + toISOString)
findings.evidence: iso(days) does d.setDate(d.getDate()+days) on local time then d.toISOString().slice(0,10), i.e. the UTC date.
findings.failure_scenario: A Denver purchaser logs a call at 19:00 MDT choosing 'in a week': the UTC date is already tomorrow, so nextFollowUpAt is 8 days out (and the chip shows that date); a Shenzhen user before 08:00 gets 6 days. The follow-up list drifts.
findings.proposed_fix: Format the local date (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) or use the shared todayIn/addDays helpers with the reporting TZ.
findings.regression_test: Fake timers at 2026-10-31T01:30:00Z with TZ=America/Denver; assert iso(7) === '2026-11-06'.

findings.title: Dashboard trend chip shows the wrong direction when the previous period's profit was negative
findings.evidence: delta = ((current - prev) / prev) * 100 with no Math.abs on the denominator; TrendChip is used for profit (line 97).
findings.failure_scenario: Previous period gross profit -$1,000, this period +$500: delta = 1500/-1000 = -150%, rendered as a red down arrow '150% vs last period' although profit improved.
findings.proposed_fix: Divide by Math.abs(prev).
findings.regression_test: Render TrendChip current=500 prev=-1000 and assert class 'up'.

findings.title: Members: 'Revoke' deactivates a member with no confirm, and the remove confirm is not busy-guarded
findings.evidence: Pending-invite Revoke calls removeMember(inv) directly (DELETE /api/members/:id = deactivate, which also ends sessions), while the row trash button goes through ConfirmDialog. removeMember has no in-flight flag and ConfirmDialog is rendered without busy (line 257-264), so a double click on Remove sends two DELETEs.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager clicks Revoke next to the wrong pending email and the member is deactivated immediately; double-clicking Remove produces a success toast followed by an error toast for the second request.
findings.proposed_fix: Route Revoke through setRemoving(inv); add a removing-in-flight state passed as ConfirmDialog busy and checked in removeMember.
findings.regression_test: Click Revoke and assert api.delete not called before confirm; double-click confirm and assert one DELETE.

findings.title: One-time secrets (new host token, invited member temp password) are lost by a stray close
findings.evidence: AddHostDialog: Modal onClose={() => { if (!busy) onClose(); }} also applies to the 'created' step that shows the bearer token 'once and never again' (fleetHostTokenOnce), so Escape/backdrop dismisses it. MembersPanel InviteMemberModal (settings/MembersPanel.tsx:377,463) wires Cancel/X straight to onClose even while saving, so closing mid-request drops the temp password the POST returns (and skips the list reload).
findings.failure_scenario: Manager registers a host, clicks outside the modal before copying: the token is gone and the host has to be removed and re-added. Same for an invite closed while 'Sending': the member exists but nobody has their password.
findings.proposed_fix: On the token/password step, ignore backdrop/Escape (only Done closes); disable Cancel/X while saving in InviteMemberModal.
findings.regression_test: Render AddHostDialog in created state, fire Escape, assert onClose not called.

findings.title: Box check: Escape (and the drawer backdrop) silently discards an edited line
findings.evidence: useEscapeKey(() => { if (editing) setEditing(null); ... }) drops `editing` regardless of editing.line._dirty; LineDrawer's backdrop onClick={onClose} (submit/LineDrawer.tsx:276) does the same. The page has no useUnsavedGuard for the drawer either.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager corrects qty/serials of a line that arrived different, presses Escape to dismiss an autocomplete or clicks beside the drawer: all edits are gone with no prompt.
findings.proposed_fix: When editing.line._dirty, ask before closing (Escape/backdrop), and register useUnsavedGuard(!!editing?.line._dirty).
findings.regression_test: Open the drawer, change qty, fire Escape, assert the drawer stays open (or a confirm appears).

findings.title: Reddit leads: a failed list load leaves the skeleton up forever
findings.evidence: load = leadsApi.list().then(r => setLeads(r.leads), handleFetchError); on rejection leads stays null and body renders <TableSkeleton> (line 155) with no retry.
findings.failure_scenario: Tracker/API blip on open: the error dialog is dismissed and the Pool/My leads tabs show a loading skeleton indefinitely until a full reload.
findings.proposed_fix: Track a failed state and render an error row with a Retry calling load().
findings.regression_test: Mock leadsApi.list to reject; assert a retry control renders instead of the skeleton.

findings.title: Web submission reply draft is lost on navigation without a prompt
findings.evidence: draft is plain component state; SubmissionThread is keyed by submission id (DesktopWebSubmissions.tsx:437) and has no useUnsavedGuard, unlike other editors (DesktopSellOrders, DesktopInternalTxns, FleetFlow).
findings.failure_scenario: A manager types a long reply to a customer, clicks another submission or nav item: the reply vanishes.
findings.proposed_fix: useUnsavedGuard(draft.trim().length > 0) in SubmissionThread.
findings.regression_test: Type into the composer, navigate, assert the leave prompt.

findings.title: Account pool sort headers are mouse-only
findings.evidence: <th className='fp-th-sort' onClick={() => sortBy(i)}> with aria-sort but no button/tabIndex/onKeyDown.
findings.failure_scenario: Keyboard users cannot sort the manager table by status, holder or cookie age.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the header label in a <button type='button'> that calls sortBy(i).
findings.regression_test: Tab to a header and press Enter; assert sort changes.

findings.title: Deleting a tracked package is one click with no confirmation
findings.evidence: The 'Remove' button calls remove() -> removePackage(pkg.id) immediately (lines 301-311); backend packages.delete('/:id') (apps/backend/src/routes/packages.ts:372) hard-DELETEs the row. It sits beside the 'Refresh' ghost button of identical size in the same cell.
findings.failure_scenario: A user aiming for Refresh on a standalone package clicks Remove; the tracking number, seller name, note, source and PayPal txn link vanish with no undo, and the box later arrives with nothing to create its PO from.
findings.proposed_fix: Route the click through ConfirmDialog (danger) naming the tracking number, or offer an Undo toast.
findings.regression_test: Component test: click Remove, assert removePackage not called until the confirm button is pressed.

findings.title: Activity register stays on the skeleton forever after a failed first load
findings.evidence: The debounced effect does setFeed(null) then api.get(...).then(setFeed).catch(handleFetchError); nothing sets feed on failure, so `feed === null` keeps rendering <ListSkeleton> (line 391) and the footer says 'Loading' (line 544) indefinitely.
findings.failure_scenario: Backend hiccup or a 500 on /api/activity: the user dismisses the error dialog and is left with a permanent loading skeleton and no retry; changing a filter is the only way out.
findings.proposed_fix: Track an error state (e.g. feed = 'error') and render an error row with a Retry button; or keep the previous feed and only clear it on success.
findings.regression_test: Mock api.get to reject; assert skeleton is replaced by an error/retry element after the promise settles.

findings.title: Inventory activity drawer: pill counts are computed from the filtered, 200-capped result; errors render as 'no events'; no stale-response guard
findings.evidence: counts is derived from `events` (lines 64-71), which the server already filtered by `kind` and capped at LIMIT 200 (apps/backend/src/routes/inventory.ts ~621). The fetch effect (49-59) has .catch(() => setEvents([])) and no request-id check, unlike DesktopActivity's reqId.
findings.failure_scenario: Pick 'Priced': every other pill drops to 0 and 'All' shows the priced count; with a busy log 'All' never exceeds 200. A network/500 error shows 'No events match' with no toast. Typing a search where an earlier slower request returns last shows the older query's rows under the newer text.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the endpoint return per-kind counts (as /api/activity does) or hide counts when filtered; surface errors via handleFetchError; guard with a monotonically increasing request id.
findings.regression_test: Mock two overlapping fetches resolving out of order and assert the later query's rows win; mock reject and assert handleFetchError called.

findings.title: Stock analysis margin KPI renders '+-12%' and '▲ $-1,234' when sell value is below cost
findings.evidence: value={'+' + pct(sell - cost, cost) + '%'} and sub=▲ {money(sell - cost)} hard-code the plus sign, the up arrow and the positive colour; money() is '$' + Math.round(n).toLocaleString() so negatives print '$-1,234'. The per-type section meta (line 246) does the same with `+${margin}%`.
findings.failure_scenario: A warehouse/category slice whose listings are priced under cost (or unpriced lots counted at 0 sell) shows a green '▲ +-35%' margin, misreporting a loss.
findings.proposed_fix: Format the sign from the value (Intl.NumberFormat signDisplay:'exceptZero'), pick an arrow/colour by sign, and format money negatives as -$1,234.
findings.regression_test: Render DesktopAnalysis with value {cost:1000, sell:800} and assert text '-20%' and no 'an-pos'.

findings.title: Submit page's two hand-rolled dialogs (existing-draft choice, part-number confirm) have no Escape, focus trap or dialog role
findings.evidence: The choice dialog (1293) and pnConfirm dialog (1396) are bare <div className="modal-backdrop"> instead of components/Modal: no role=dialog/aria-modal, no useFocusTrap, no Escape entry on the stack. The drawer's Escape handler (677-680) returns early whenever a .modal-backdrop exists, so Escape does nothing while they are open.
findings.failure_scenario: Keyboard user presses Submit, the 'add to existing PO?' dialog opens: Escape is ignored, Tab walks into the page behind the backdrop, and screen readers do not announce a dialog.
findings.proposed_fix: Render both with <Modal onClose=... ariaLabel=...> (guarding onClose while submitting), as DupPartDialog already does.
findings.regression_test: Component test: open the choice dialog, dispatch Escape, assert it closes; assert role='dialog' present.

findings.title: Merging into an existing draft writes otherFees from a snapshot taken at page mount (lost update)
findings.evidence: allDrafts is fetched once on mount (line 276). doSubmitToExisting sends otherFees: target.otherFees + parseFeeInput(meta.otherFees), an absolute value computed from that snapshot, not a server-side increment.
findings.failure_scenario: Purchaser opens Submit, meanwhile the target draft's fees are edited (another tab, or a manager adds a $40 shipping fee). The merge PATCH writes the stale fee + this batch's fee, silently erasing the $40.
findings.proposed_fix: Send the delta (e.g. addOtherFees) and let the backend add it inside the PATCH transaction, or re-read the target right before the PATCH.
findings.regression_test: Backend/route test: PATCH with an addOtherFees delta against a row whose fee changed after the client read it; assert sum preserved.

findings.title: Trial-prompt editor discards a long edited prompt on Escape or a backdrop click
findings.evidence: CandidateModal holds a 14-row prompt textarea in local state and passes onClose straight to <Modal>, which closes on Escape and backdrop click (components/Modal.tsx). No dirty check or useUnsavedGuard.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager spends minutes rewriting the evaluator prompt, presses Escape to dismiss the model picker menu (or mis-clicks outside the shell): the modal closes and the rewrite is gone.
findings.proposed_fix: When prompt/model differ from the initial values, ask via confirmDiscard() (lib/unsavedGuard) before closing, and register useUnsavedGuard(dirty).
findings.regression_test: Component test: type into the textarea, fire Escape, assert the modal is still open and a discard confirm was requested.

findings.title: Tracker confirm dialogs (Promote, End trial, Delete subreddit) don't pass busy, so a double click fires the request twice
findings.evidence: ConfirmDialog supports busy (settings/dialogs.tsx:6) but these callers never set it; onConfirm fires promoteCandidate()/clearCandidate()/deleteSubreddit() and closes only in .finally. Tracker POST /api/prompt-candidate/promote returns 400 'no candidate_eval_prompt is set' once the first call cleared it; DELETE /api/subreddits/:name returns 404 the second time (trackers/reddit/src/api.ts:179-184). Same pattern at DesktopTracker.tsx:218-234.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager double-clicks Promote: the prompt is promoted, a 'Promoted' toast shows, then an error dialog says no candidate is set, suggesting the promotion failed.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep a pending flag, pass busy to ConfirmDialog and ignore onConfirm while pending.
findings.regression_test: Component test: click confirm twice synchronously; assert promoteCandidate called once.

findings.title: Lead follow-up date input saves on every keystroke, writing bogus years and history rows
findings.evidence: <input type="date" value={lead.followUp ?? ''} onChange={e => void act(leadsApi.followUp(lead.username, e.target.value || null))} /> has no busy guard or commit-on-blur. Typing the year in Chrome's date field yields valid intermediate values (0002-, 0020-, 0202-, 2026-...), each passing the backend check (/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ + Date.parse, apps/backend/src/routes/redditLeads.ts:323) and each writing a follow_up event.
findings.failure_scenario: Purchaser types a date: four PUTs land, the history shows four follow-up changes including year 0002, and if responses arrive out of order the lead is left with follow_up 0202-11-05, i.e. permanently overdue.
findings.proposed_fix: Commit on blur/Enter (or debounce) and only when the year is plausible (>= current year); disable while busy.
findings.regression_test: Component test: fire change events with 0002-11-05 then 2026-11-05 quickly; assert one followUp call with the final value.

findings.title: Client preferences (shipping, contact) are stored as the editor's translated label
findings.evidence: Picker computes text = translate ? t(o) : o and saves onPick(text), so prefLogistics/prefContact persist 'They ship' or '他寄件' depending on the editor's language (keys cliShipThey etc., i18n.zh.ts:1158). ClientDrawer.tsx:149-150 prints the raw stored string. The file header says pickers exist so the value can be filtered on.
findings.failure_scenario: A Chinese-locale manager sets shipping to '他寄件'; an English user sees '他寄件' in the drawer, and in Edit no option is highlighted (value !== t(o)); filters/reports cannot group the two spellings.
findings.proposed_fix: Store the stable key (cliShipThey...) and translate on display; migrate existing values by mapping both dictionaries back to keys.
findings.regression_test: Unit test: render EditClient with lang zh, pick a shipping option, assert PATCH body prefLogistics === 'cliShipThey'.

findings.title: Categories panel: 'Add category' button does nothing; clearing default margin saves 0%
findings.evidence: actions={<button className="btn">...catAddBtn</button>} has no onClick. The margin input does upd(defaultMargin: Number(e.target.value)) and persists on blur (100-101); an emptied field gives Number('') = 0 and is PATCHed.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager clicks 'Add category' and nothing happens. Manager clears the margin field to retype it and tabs away: the category's default margin is saved as 0%.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the button (or wire it), and on blur skip persisting when the field is empty/NaN, restoring the last saved value.
findings.regression_test: Component test: clear margin input and blur; assert no PATCH with defaultMargin 0.

'anon'} />, so the shell (editingOrder, loadingOrderId, orderReloads) remounts on every real identity change, and late responses land on the unmounted instance.
